'''Cristina Dorador Ortiz''' (born February 28, 1980, in [[Antofagasta]]) is a [[Chile]]an [[scientist]], doctor, and former assembly member of the Chilean [[Constitutional convention (political meeting)|Constitutional Convention]] who conducts research in [[microbiology]], microbial [[ecology]], [[limnology]] and geomicrobiology. She is also an associate professor in the department of biotechnology of the Faculty of Marine Sciences and Natural Resources at the [[University of Antofagasta]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.uantof.cl/departamentos/biotecnologia |title=Departamento Biotecnología |access-date=20 March 2020 |author=Universidad de Antofagasta |website=www.uantof.cl |archive-date=20 March 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200320014422/http://www.uantof.cl/departamentos/biotecnologia |url-status=dead }}</ref>

She coordinates in Chile of the Extreme Environment Network for the study of ecosystems in the geographical extremes of Chile<ref name=NEXER>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nexerchile.cl/|title=Network for Extreme Environment Research|access-date=6 March 2020|language=en-US}}</ref> and has developed biotechnological tools to value the unique properties of some highland microbial communities such as resistance to [[ultraviolet]] radiation for elaborate cosmetic creams, joining the field of [[:es:Biotecnología cosmética|cosmetic biotechnology]]. She has also led the development of textile material using the photoprotective properties of highland bacteria.

She was a member of the transition council of the [[CONICYT|National Commission for Scientific and Technological Research]] in 2019 that gave rise to the [[:es:Agencia Nacional de Investigación y Desarrollo de Chile|National Agency for Research and Development of Chile]], and has been recognized nationally and internationally as one of the most relevant researchers in Chile.<ref>{{Cite news |title=EyN: 100 Mujeres Líderes 2017 |url=http://www.economiaynegocios.cl/noticias/noticias.asp?id=423072 |date=4 December 2017 |access-date=20 March 2020 |website=El Mercurio}}</ref>

From July 2021 to July 2022, she served as a [[Constitutional Convention (Chile)|conventional constituent]] for District 3, which represents the [[Antofagasta Region]].

==Biography==
Cristina Dorador was born in Antofagasta in 1980, where she spent her childhood and completed her primary and secondary studies. She later obtained her degree in biology from the [[:es:Facultad de Ciencias de la Universidad de Chile|Faculty of Sciences]] at the [[University of Chile]] in [[Santiago]]. She then did a Ph.D. at the [[University of Kiel]] in Germany and the [[Max Planck Society|Max Planck Institute]] for Limnology in [[Plön]] and obtained a job at the University of Antofagasta.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Meléndez |first=Soledad |title=Mujer de ciencia |url=https://old.tell.cl/magazine/13398/antofagasta/julio/2014/entrevistas/mujer-de-ciencia.html |date=July 2014 |access-date=20 March 2020 |publisher=Tell Magazine |language=es}}</ref>

She is the daughter of teacher and poet Wilfredo Dorador and Milena Ortiz, also a teacher. She formed her family with the English researcher Chris Harrod with whom she has two children.

==Education and scientific activities==
Dorador is a biologist from the [[University of Chile]]. She subsequently obtained her Ph.D. in Natural Sciences with a minor in microbiology at the Christian-Albrechts Universität zu Kiel in [[Kiel]], Germany in 2007.

She has studied ecosystems of the highland salt flats system, investigating the importance of microbes for the extreme systems of the [[Atacama Desert]].<ref>{{Cite journal |url=https://link.springer.com/10.1007/s10482-019-01328-x |title=Atacama Database: a platform of the microbiome of the Atacama Desert |last1=Contador |first1=Carolina A. |last2=Veas-Castillo |first2=Luis |date= February 2020 |journal=Antonie van Leeuwenhoek |volume=113 |issue=2 |pages=185–195 |access-date=11 March 2020 |language=en |issn=0003-6072 |doi=10.1007/s10482-019-01328-x |last3=Tapia |first3=Emilio |last4=Antipán |first4=Marcela |last5=Miranda |first5=Noemi |last6=Ruiz-Tagle |first6=Benjamín |last7=García-Araya |first7=Jonathan |last8=Andrews |first8=Barbara A. |last9=Marin |first9=Mauricio|pmid=31535335 |s2cid=202672082 |url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Dorador has described the ability of bacteria to degrade synthetic compounds such as polyesters and plastics. She has also highlighted the microbial diversity at high altitudes and the properties that make them resistant to extreme conditions. The microbial activity of salt flats in northern Chile is today a relevant issue for the biological heritage of Chile thanks to the field studies carried out by Dorador and her team in the last 10 years.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://accounts.google.com/Login?hl=es&continue=https://scholar.google.com/citations%3Fhl%3Des%26amp%3Buser%3DJGCbLoIAAAAJ%26amp%3Bview_op%3Dlist_works&service=citations|title=Citas de Google Académico|access-date=6 March 2020|website=accounts.google.com}}</ref>

===Scientific dissemination===
She has been a scientific advisor to the PAR Explora Antofagasta program of the National Commission for Scientific and Technological Research and participated in other dissemination bodies such as Puerto de Ideas, [[:es:Congreso Futuro|Congreso Futuro]]<ref>«Cristina Dorador - Congreso Futuro». congresofuturo.cl. Consultado el 6 de marzo de 2020.</ref> and [[TED (conference)|TEDx]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ted.com/tedx/events/17962|title=TEDxSantiago - TED|access-date=6 March 2020|website=www.ted.com}}</ref> In parallel, she is a columnist in the Chilean scientific dissemination blog Ethylmercury.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.etilmercurio.com/em/quienes-somos/ |title=¿Quiénes somos? |access-date=11 March 2020 |author=etilmercurio |language=es-CL}}</ref> She is a member of the [[:es:Asociación Red de Investigadoras|Asociación Red de Investigadoras]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://redinvestigadoras.cl/miembros/cristina-dorador-ortiz/|title=Cristina Dorador Ortiz – Red de investigadoras|date=30 August 2019 |access-date=1 April 2020|language=es-CL}}</ref>

==Politics==
She was registered as an independent candidate in the [[2021 Chilean Constitutional Convention election|2021 conventional constituent elections]] for district 3 (Calama, María Elena, Ollagüe, San Pedro de Atacama, Tocopilla, Antofagasta, Mejillones, Sierra Gorda and Taltal), forming part of the independent movement of the north.<ref>{{cite web |title=Constituyentes por una lucha: Estos son los candidatos que defienden el medio ambiente |url=https://www.duna.cl/noticias/2021/02/26/constituyentes-por-una-lucha-estos-son-los-candidatos-que-defienden-el-medio-ambiente/ |publisher=Radio Duna |date=26 February 2021 |access-date=3 March 2021}}</ref> She was elected with 12.68% of the votes, reaching the first majority of the district.<ref>{{cite web |title=¿Qué piensan los independientes electos para la Convención?: Zoom a sus programas |url=https://www.emol.com/noticias/Nacional/2021/05/17/1021076/que-piensan-independientes-convencion-constitucional.html |publisher=Emol |date=17 May 2021 |access-date=17 May 2021}}</ref>

==Awards and distinctions==
Dorador is a member of the international panel of the international society for microbial ecology.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.isme-microbes.org/|title=International Society for Microbial Ecology|author=ISME|access-date=6 March 2020|website=www.isme-microbes.org}}</ref> and she was a member of the transition council of the [[CONICYT|National Commission for Scientific and Technological Research]] in 2019 that gave rise to the [[:es:Agencia Nacional de Investigación y Desarrollo de Chile|National Research and Development Agency of Chile]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Pasten |first=David |title=Dra. Cristina Dorador integra el Consejo para la transición de CONICYT |url=http://www.comunicacionesua.cl/2019/06/04/dra-cristina-dorador-integra-el-consejo-para-la-transicion-de-conicyt/ |date=4 June 2019 |access-date=20 March 2020 |publisher=Comunicaciones UA |language=es-ES}}</ref>

According to the report "Ciencias Imagen Chile" developed by Marca Chile in 2018, Dorador is among the most prominent Chilean researchers in international media.<ref>Marcha Chile (mayo de 2018). «Ciencia y Tecnología de Chile En la prensa internacional / 2017». Consultado el 20 de marzo de 2020.</ref> She was also chosen in 2017 as one of the 100 leading women in the country by [[El Mercurio]].

Her commitment to the communities of northern Chile was reflected in the laboratory that bears her name at the Liceo Radomiro Tomic in [[Calama, Chile|Calama]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.comdescalama.cl/liceo-radomiro-tomic-inauguro-su-laboratorio-de-ciencias/ |title=Corporación Municipal de Desarrollo Social de Calama »  |access-date=20 March 2020 |author=LICEO RADOMIRO TOMIC INAUGURÓ SU LABORATORIO DE CIENCIAS |date=17 August 2019}}</ref> Cristina was the representative of Chile as a young scientist in the book “Young Scientists. A bright future for the Americas,"<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.conicyt.cl/blog/2016/04/12/jovenes-cientificas-un-futuro-brillante-para-las-americas/|title="Jóvenes científicas: Un futuro Brillante para las Américas"|author=CONICYT|access-date=6 March 2020|website=www.conicyt.cl}}</ref> published by the [[InterAmerican Network of Academies of Sciences]].
